summary: Postinstall and import-time beacon exfiltrates host metadata to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package ships a `beacon.cjs` that POSTs installer hostname, install path, current working directory, Node.js version, and package name to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc over plain HTTP. The beacon fires both from a `postinstall` lifecycle hook (`node beacon.cjs`) and at import time from `index.js`. The `index.js` module itself is a Proxy stub that no-ops every property access, so the only real effect of installing or requiring the package is the outbound beacon. There is no advertised functionality, no first-party relationship to the destination IP, and no opt-in; an in-file comment framing the collection as benign metadata does not change the behavior. The package name and scope (`@wxwxtest/testrrrdd`) and the callback-only shim shape are consistent with a dependency-confusion or typosquat reconnaissance payload.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
